question:
A cooperative society has 50 hectares of land available for growing two crops X and Y. One hectare of crop X requires 2 units of irrigation and 1 unit of labour, while one hectare of crop Y requires 1 unit of irrigation and 2 units of labour. At most 80 units of irrigation and 70 units of labour are available. The profit earned is Rs 5000 per hectare from crop X and Rs 4000 per hectare from crop Y. Let $x$ and $y$ represent the hectares allocated to X and Y respectively. The society wants to maximise its total profit by analysing the restrictions graphically.

(a) Form all the linear constraints for the allocation problem.

(b) Show that the boundary lines for land, irrigation and labour meet at the common point $(30,20)$.

(c) The graphical analysis gives the corner points $(0,0)$, $(40,0)$, $(30,20)$ and $(0,35)$. Calculate the total profit at each point.

(d) Determine the optimal allocation and explain which available resources are completely utilised at that allocation.
explanation:
(a)
The total land available is 50 hectares, so
$$x+y\leq 50$$

The irrigation requirement is 2 units per hectare for X and 1 unit per hectare for Y. Hence,
$$2x+y\leq 80$$

The labour requirement is 1 unit per hectare for X and 2 units per hectare for Y. Hence,
$$x+2y\leq 70$$

Also,
$$x\geq 0,\quad y\geq 0$$

These are the required constraints.

(b)
At $(30,20)$, the land boundary gives
$$30+20=50$$
The irrigation boundary gives
$$2(30)+20=80$$
The labour boundary gives
$$30+2(20)=70$$
Thus, $(30,20)$ lies on all three boundary lines and is their common point.

(c)
The objective function for total profit is
$$Z=5000x+4000y$$

At $(0,0)$,
$$Z=0$$
At $(40,0)$,
$$Z=5000(40)=200000$$
At $(30,20)$,
$$Z=5000(30)+4000(20)=150000+80000=230000$$
At $(0,35)$,
$$Z=4000(35)=140000$$

(d)
The greatest value of $Z$ is Rs 230000 at $(30,20)$. Therefore, 30 hectares should be allocated to crop X and 20 hectares to crop Y.

At this allocation, land used is $30+20=50$ hectares, irrigation used is $2(30)+20=80$ units, and labour used is $30+2(20)=70$ units. Hence, all the available land, irrigation and labour are completely utilised.

options.A:
(a) $x+y\leq50$, $2x+y\leq80$, $x+2y\leq70$, $x,y\geq0$
(b) $(30,20)$ satisfies only the land and irrigation boundaries
(c) Maximum profit Rs $200000$ at $(40,0)$
(d) Only land and irrigation are completely utilised
options.B:
(a) $x+y\leq50$, $2x+y\leq80$, $x+2y\leq70$, $x,y\geq0$
(b) $(30,20)$ lies on all three boundary lines
(c) Profits at $(0,0),(40,0),(30,20),(0,35)$ are Rs $0,200000,230000,140000$ respectively
(d) Allocate $30$ hectares to X and $20$ hectares to Y; all three resources are completely utilised
options.C:
(a) $x+y\geq50$, $2x+y\leq80$, $x+2y\leq70$, $x,y\geq0$
(b) $(30,20)$ lies on all three boundaries
(c) Maximum profit Rs $230000$ at $(30,20)$
(d) Only irrigation and labour are completely utilised
options.D:
(a) $x+y\leq50$, $x+2y\leq80$, $2x+y\leq70$, $x,y\geq0$
(b) $(30,20)$ is not on all three boundaries
(c) Maximum profit Rs $220000$ at $(30,20)$
(d) Allocate $20$ hectares to X and $30$ hectares to Y
